syllabus_topics: 2nd order differential equations. Strong and weak formulation. Galerkin approximation.
1D problems: Domain discretization. Finite element and shape function. Linear, quadratic and higher order elements. Applications: One-dimensional bars; Heat Transfer; Laminar flow. Discrete systems.
Finite elements for planar trusses. Beam element. Frames. Beam-bar element.

2D problems: Triangular and quadrangular finite elements. Linear and quadratic interpolation functions. Standard element. Coordinate transformation. Numerical integration. Isoparametric elements. Applications: Heat transfer; Potential flow; Torsion in a non-circular section shaft; Deformation of elastic membranes. Finite elements in two-dimensional elasticity.
Error estimates. Modeling considerations: Error sources, admissible elements, mesh refinement. Extension to 3D problems. Implementation of an FE program. Commercial FE software.
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on two computational assignments (25% each) and two tests (25% each). A minimum average grade of 8 must be achieved in the tests. The assessment method, including the grades from assignments, applies to resit and special examinations, which are make-up exams for the two tests.
bibliography: J.N Reddy, "Introduction to the Finite Element Method", 4th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2018 (main)
